description: Screenshot of the 'Minimal wxWidgets App' sample window after the paint handler calls dc.SetTransformMatrix() (translate 40,75 / scale 2,3) and then dc.DestroyClippingRegion(). The yellow background fill (drawn by dc.Clear() with a yellow brush) only covers a small rectangle offset from the client-area origin instead of the full client area, showing that the clipping region left in place after DestroyClippingRegion() is wrong (too small and positioned incorrectly) when a custom transform matrix is active. Only the rendered window chrome (title bar, menu, yellow fill, status bar) is visible in the pixels -- there is no debug-log panel, console output, or file path/URL/API-name text baked into the image itself; the SetTransformMatrix/DestroyClippingRegion details above are reviewer-only context reconstructed from the upstream issue, not something visible in the screenshot.

Screenshot of the same sample window, but with the paint handler's else-branch taken instead: logical coordinates are changed with SetDeviceOrigin()/SetUserScale()/SetLogicalScale()/SetLogicalOrigin() rather than SetTransformMatrix(). After the same dc.DestroyClippingRegion() call, the yellow background fill correctly covers the entire client area. As with bug.png, only the rendered window chrome is visible in the pixels -- no debug-log panel, console text, or code-level identifiers appear in the image. This is the correct/expected rendering that the transform-matrix case in bug.png should also produce once the clip region is properly reset.
